title: Cantor Fitzgerald technology analyst to hold analyst/industry conference call AMZN;GOOGL;GOOG;AAPL;MSFT - The Fly
text:
Game On: Activision begins 'Battle' pre-purchase, 'Call of Duty' playoffs start » Welcome to "Game… 
Welcome to "Game On," The Fly's weekly recap of the stories powering up or beating down video game stocks. ACTIVISION BEGINS 'BATTLE' PRE-PURCHASE, PLANS 'SPYRO' RELEASE: On Thursday, Activision Blizzard (ATVI) announced World of Warcraft players can now pre-purchase Battle for Azeroth, the seventh expansion for Blizzard Entertainment's massive multiplayer online role-playing game. In addition to gaining a level-110 character boost to use immediately, players who pre-purchase can begin their journey to recruit the first four of the expansion's new Allied Races. The company also said anyone interested in joining the fight with the next expansion can pre-purchase Battle for Azeroth digitally through the Blizzard Shop and receive the current expansion, Legion, for free. Additionally on Thursday, Activision confirmed that it is releasing a collection of remastered editions of its first three "Spyro the Dragon" games on September 21. The collection, named "Spyro: Reignited Trilogy," will include updated versions of "Spyro the Dragon,""Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage," and "Spyro: Year of the Dragon." The game collection will launch on Xbox One (MSFT) and PlayStation 4 (SNE) consoles. CALL OF DUTY PLAYOFFS START: On Friday, The Call of Duty World League is entered its first stage finals with the top eight teams from the CWL Pro League Stage 1 facing off. At stake is the winner's share of a $500,000 event prize pool and the role of early season favorite in the 2018 season of the CWL, which features a $4.2M total prize purse. The CWL Pro League Stage 1 Playoffs is presented by PlayStation 4 and the finals will see top teams from North America and Europe compete in "Call of Duty: WWII," from Activision Publishing on PlayStation 4 through Sunday, April 8. Viewers can watch the broadcast on MLG.com/CallofDuty and on Twitch (AMZN). Matches will also be available to watch via the in-game "Call of Duty: WWII" theater within Headquarters on PlayStation 4. OVERBLOWN RISK: On Friday, Piper Jaffray analyst Michael Olson said shares of Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) are down 10% year and have lagged video game peers Activision Blizzard and Electronic Arts (EA) due to concerns around "Fortnite" and disappointment with December quarter digital revenue. The shares should be bought at current levels as "Fortnite" risk is overblown, Olson said. The analyst's conversations with major video game publishers suggest the potential impact from "Fortnite" has been "blown out of proportion." While the analyst does expect a measurable impact on Activision's near-term revenue due to overlapping titles, he sees "very minimal impact" on EA and Take-Two. Further, Olson believes Take Two has a "significant catalyst" in October with Red Dead Redemption. He views the stock's relative valuation as discounted and reiterates an Overweight rating on the shares with a $127 price target. PULLBACKS A BUYING OPPORTUNITY: On Wednesday, KeyBanc analyst Evan Wingren reduced estimates for Activision Blizzard, Electronic Arts, and Take-Two, but said he views the pullbacks as a meaningful buying opportunity. A proprietary survey, proprietary credit card analysis on sentiment, and conversations with investors and publishers lead him to believe that Fortnite will impact results. The analyst sees some room for more modest downside from here, but believes a reasonable downside scenario is priced in. ATVI
